verdict.summary: Round 10 finds no correctness, soundness, test-validity, or security defect. The diagnostic remains restricted to the already-failed parse path, returns the rejected SPARQL byte-for-byte, and never changes execution. The scanner excludes strings, IRIs, comments, variables, numeric literals, and the Unicode, escaped, empty-prefix, and dotted prefixed-name forms implicated by earlier review rounds; hint count, candidate processing, ordering, and deduplication are deterministic and bounded. The public error-contract tests exercise the real transpilation/canary path, prove non-application, cover hint-free failures, and reproduce the prefixed-name regressions. The keyword drift guard and the documentation's explicitly unmeasured, diagnostic-only framing agree with the implementation. Round 9 likewise had no findings, so progress is stagnant under the required scale.
